description:
FOUND s507 (Fable, 2026-10-04) by the quick companion leg run on s506f's final tree (which carries main): op/utf8cache.t differs from its snapshot (OK 16/0 -> DIFF 14/2, parallel and serial agree; rows 13 "no utf8 pos cache on globs" and 15 "no utf8 length cache on globs").  ATTRIBUTED by running the file alone: 618db500 OK 16/0, main d23b5927 DIFF 14/2 -- the full companion run of 2e71d4aa earlier the same evening had it OK, so it is s502e (#2056), merged as d23b5927.  My review of s502e ran no op/ companion leg (its brief asked for io/ only) -- the standing rule "a cl/ coercion / dereference change runs the op/ companion leg" (s421) was not applied.  The snapshot row is NOT spliced: it stays OK 16/0 until this is fixed.

THE CAUSE (read): s502e added to `p-cast-$` (read and setf, cl/pcl-runtime.lisp) the arm `((p-typeglob-p inner) (p-box-value (%p-glob-scalar-box inner)))` -- "`${*$fh}`: a GLOB's SCALAR slot" -- which is right when the operand IS a glob (`${*foo}`, `${*$fh}`, `${*{$ref}}`, and a glob VALUE held in a scalar: `my $g = *foo; $$g`) and wrong when the operand is a REFERENCE to a glob: perl's `$$globref` is the glob itself.

PROBE (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s507/review/g1-globref.pl; outputs out/g1.perl / g1.main / g1.618db500; `our $foo = "sv"; our @foo = (1, 2); my $gr = \*foo;`):
  row  expression                                   perl                 618db500 (before)     main d23b5927
  01   "$$gr", length($$gr)                         *main::foo 10        *main::foo 10         sv 2            <- REGRESSED
  02   ${*foo} / ${*{$gr}} / ${*$gr}                sv sv sv             *main::foo x3         sv sv sv        <- s502e FIXED these
  04   ${$gr}                                       *main::foo           *main::foo            sv              <- REGRESSED
  05   my $copy = $$gr; ref(\$copy)                 *main::foo GLOB      *main::foo GLOB       sv SCALAR       <- REGRESSED
  06   *{$$gr} = \"new"; $foo                       new                  new                   sv              <- REGRESSED
  07   open my $fh…; ${*$fh} = "p"; ${*$fh}{k} = "v"   p v               (died)                p v             <- s502e FIXED
  10   my $sr = \*STDOUT; fileno($$sr); $$sr eq "*main::STDOUT"   fileno name   (not reached)  nofileno, ""    <- wrong on main
THE DISCRIMINATOR EXISTS at run time (measured, g2.pl): `my $g = *foo; my $gr = \*foo;` -- PCL answers `ref($g)` "" and `ref($gr)` "GLOB" exactly as perl does, and `$$g` (a glob VALUE) is "sv" in both.  So the fix is ONE condition on s502e's arm, in both the reader and the setf: it applies when the operand is a glob VALUE, not when it is a reference to a glob (whatever `ref` reads to tell them apart); a reference to a glob falls through to the arm that returns the referent, as before d23b5927.
ACCEPTANCE: every row of g1-globref.pl identical to perl (rows 02 and 07 must STAY fixed); op/utf8cache.t OK 16/0 again; the everyday row modules/File-Temp stays `same`; the s502e guard rows (Pl/t/transpile-test-10.t 78-80) still pass; a new guard row for rows 01 / 05 / 06 / 10 that fails on main d23b5927.  Then the op/ and uni/ companion legs BEFORE / AFTER (op/gv.t and uni/gv.t are TIMEOUT files a quick run does not compare: read their row counts by hand).
subject: REGRESSION on main since d23b5927 (s502e #2056, found by Fable's companion leg on the next batch): `$$globref` -- dereferencing a REFERENCE to a glob with `$` -- yields the glob's SCALAR slot; perl yields the GLOB (`*main::foo`).  op/utf8cache.t OK 16/0 -> DIFF 14/2; `fileno($$ref)`, `*{$$ref} = …`, `my $copy = $$ref` are all wrong
